title: Exact trig values
cover_sub: No calculator, no rounding. Secure the values for 0°, 30°, 45°, 60° and 90°, extend to finding sides and angles exactly, then master surd answers in real shapes.

levels_long.s: Recall the exact values and combine them.
levels_long.e: Exact sides and angles in right-angled triangles, and tampered evidence.
levels_long.m: Surd answers in shapes, and simple trig equations.

briefing: On the non-calculator paper you must know these values by heart. They come from two triangles: half an equilateral triangle (30° and 60°) and half a square (45°).

0°30°45°60°90°
sin012√22√321
cos1√32√22120
tan01√31√3–
method: Learn the table, or rebuild it from the two triangles.
Label the sides of the right-angled triangle: hypotenuse, opposite, adjacent.
Pick sin, cos or tan with SOH CAH TOA, and substitute the exact value.
Keep surds exact: rationalise a denominator if you're asked to simplify.

example.question: A ramp makes an angle of 30° with the ground and is 8 m long. How high does it rise? Give an exact answer.
steps: The ramp is the hypotenuse; the height is opposite the 30° angle. So use sin.
Height = 4 m. Check: 4 is half of 8, as the 30° triangle always gives ✓

questions.working: √32 × 1√3 = ½.

text: A right-angled triangle has an opposite side of 4 cm and a hypotenuse of 8 cm. Find the angle without a calculator.
Ola wrote this. Find her mistake.
questions.answer: sin 30° + sin 30° = ½ + ½ = 1, but sin 60° = √3/2. You can't add the angles.

m.blurb: No hints. Plan before you calculate.

text: An equilateral triangle has sides of 6 cm. Find its exact area.
questions.tip: Split it into two right-angled triangles with angles 30°, 60°, 90°. The height is the side opposite 60°.
